worked_examples.scenario: A man asks a Massachusetts community pharmacy for naloxone under the statewide standing order. He explains that it is for his roommate, who has recently started using opioids again and is not with him, and he hands over his own insurance card without asking to pay out-of-pocket. A technician suggests giving him the kit straight away, billing the roommate's plan once the roommate's details can be obtained, and skipping the pamphlet because the man says he has used naloxone before.
steps: Settle eligibility first. M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19(d) allows naloxone or other opioid antagonist to be prescribed and dispensed to a friend or other person in a position to assist a person at risk of experiencing an opiate-related overdose, and s. 19B(c) lets a licensed pharmacist dispense in accordance with the statewide standing order, so the roommate's absence does not prevent dispensing to the man.

Identify whose coverage is in issue. Section 19B(e) requires the pharmacist or designee to treat the transaction, for health insurance billing and cost-sharing, as the dispensing of a prescription to the person purchasing the opioid antagonist regardless of the ultimate user. The purchaser is the man, so the roommate's plan is the wrong one.

Fix the sequence. The man has not asked to pay out-of-pocket, so the pharmacist or designee shall make a reasonable effort to identify his insurance coverage and to submit a claim to his carrier prior to dispensing. Handing over the kit first and billing afterwards reverses the order the subsection sets.

Apply the counter duties. Under 247 CMR 9.06(3) the pharmacy that dispenses the kit shall provide counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet at the time of dispensing, and the regulation states no exception for a recipient who has used naloxone before.

Carry the dose forward. Under s. 19B(d) the pharmacist who dispenses an opioid antagonist annually reports to the department the number of opioid antagonist doses dispensed, and the report shall not identify an individual patient.
worked_examples.resolution: The pharmacy may dispense to the man, must make a reasonable effort to identify his own coverage and submit the claim before the kit is handed over, and must provide counseling and the pamphlet when it dispenses. The error the scenario invites is billing the ultimate user after the event, with a second error behind it: treating the recipient's experience as excusing the counseling and pamphlet duty.

worked_examples.scenario: A community pharmacy in a Massachusetts town with comparatively few overdoses dispenses its last naloxone rescue kit on a Saturday morning and has no other opioid antagonist in stock, prescription or over-the-counter. That afternoon a woman asks for a kit under the statewide standing order. The pharmacist tells her a delivery arrives on Monday and suggests she come back then. A colleague says nothing more was owed to anyone, because with no kit on hand the pharmacy had nothing to dispense, and in any case a town like theirs was never required to carry a continuous supply.
steps: Start with the pharmacy's baseline duty. Under 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) a pharmacy located in a high overdose area shall maintain a continuous supply of naloxone rescue kits or other approved opioid antagonists readily available for dispensing, and a high overdose area is one on the list the Board publishes in consultation with the Department of Public Health. The Board's Policy 2024-01 states that since all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone and must maintain a continuous, sufficient supply to meet the needs of the community, so the town's overdose numbers do not take this pharmacy outside the duty.

Recognize the stock-out as a problem of its own. Neither the regulation nor the policy states an exception for stock that runs out between deliveries, so the empty shelf is out of line with 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) and the Board's policy whatever is said to the woman.

Apply the referral duty. Under 247 CMR 9.06(4) a pharmacy that does not have a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available for dispensing at the time requested shall refer the requestor to the nearest location that has one readily available. Suggesting that she return on Monday is not a referral to the nearest location.

Add the statutory notice. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C, pharmacies located in areas with high incidence of opiate overdose, as determined by the Board in consultation with the department, shall notify the department if the supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses is insufficient to enable compliance with maintaining a continuous supply. The Board's policy states that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone in accordance with s. 19C, and a stock that is empty until Monday is such a shortfall, so notifying the department is the course to take.

Answer the colleague. The referral duty is written for the pharmacy that has nothing readily available to dispense, and the notice duty for the pharmacy whose stock is insufficient, so the absence of stock is what triggers both duties, not what excuses the pharmacy from them; and because the Board states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, the town's lower numbers do not remove the duty to keep naloxone in stock.

Keep the other duty in its place. Counseling and the pamphlet under 247 CMR 9.06(3) attach to dispensing, and nothing was dispensed to the woman, so what she was owed at this pharmacy was the referral.
worked_examples.resolution: The pharmacy owed the woman a referral to the nearest location with a kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available; on the Board's Policy 2024-01 it was also out of line with the continuous supply required of Massachusetts pharmacies, and the notice to the department that its stock was insufficient under s. 19C was the course to take. The error the scenario invites is treating a stock-out as the end of the pharmacy's obligations, or a town's lower overdose numbers as removing the duty to keep naloxone in stock, when 247 CMR 9.06(4) and s. 19C make the stock-out the start of two obligations and the Board's policy applies the stocking duty to Massachusetts pharmacies generally.

worked_examples.scenario: The manager of a pharmacy that dispenses under all three standing-order regimes circulates a compliance note. It says that every pharmacist must finish a Commissioner-approved training program before dispensing under any of the three standing orders; that the pharmacy will send the department a single report each January covering emergency contraception, opioid antagonists and COVID-19 control measures, listing each patient by name; and that COVID-19 tests need not be tracked because the reporting provision is about drugs.
steps: Test the training statement regime by regime. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19A(d) a pharmacist may complete a Commissioner-approved training program before dispensing emergency contraception; under s. 19E(c) a pharmacist shall complete a Commissioner-approved training program on COVID-19 drugs before dispensing a COVID-19 drug; and neither s. 19B nor 247 CMR 9.06 contains a training provision for dispensing an opioid antagonist.
Read the result as a statement of law. The note is right about a COVID-19 drug and overstates the law for emergency contraception and for opioid antagonists.

Test the reporting trigger. Emergency contraception and opioid antagonist reports are annual under s. 19A(e) and s. 19B(d), but s. 19E(d) requires the COVID-19 report upon request, so a January date does not govern when the department may ask for it. For naloxone the Board's Policy 2024-01 prefers reporting through the pharmacy's daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, and a pharmacy that does not report that way must email its annual report by January 15 for the previous calendar year.

Test the patient list. Reports under s. 19A(e) and s. 19B(d) shall not identify any individual patient, so naming patients in them is contrary to both provisions. Section 19E(d) does not contain that sentence; what it calls for, upon request, is a report on the doses, tests or devices dispensed.

Test the statement about tests. Under s. 19E(a) a COVID-19 control measure includes a COVID-19 test; the provision stated for a COVID-19 drug is the training proviso in s. 19E(c); and the reporting provision in s. 19E(d) reaches the doses, tests or devices dispensed, so tests are within what the department may request.

Keep the actor and the status of the reports straight. Each statutory reporting provision is written for the dispensing pharmacist, while the Board's Policy 2024-01, citing s. 19B, states that each Massachusetts pharmacy must report the number of naloxone doses dispensed, so a naloxone report made by the pharmacy follows the Board's method. In all three regimes the reports are confidential and are not public records.
worked_examples.resolution: Of the three regimes, COVID-19 drug dispensing is the one with mandatory training; emergency contraception training is permissive and the opioid antagonist provisions state no training requirement. Two regimes report annually and COVID-19 control measures upon request, tests included; the emergency contraception and opioid antagonist reports shall not identify any individual patient; and for naloxone the Board has the pharmacy report through its daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions or by an emailed report due by January 15. The error the scenario invites is assuming that one set of conditions governs every standing-order regime.

worked_examples.scenario: During an outbreak of a vaccine-preventable disease, a pharmacy chain plans a walk-in vaccination clinic. The Commissioner has not designated the vaccine or issued any order, but the chain's medical director, a registered practitioner, has signed a standing prescription for it. The plan staffs the clinic with licensed pharmacists and with pharmacy students from an accredited program, lets the students vaccinate unsupervised on busy shifts, excuses the pharmacists from training because they are licensed, limits the written protocols to storage and adverse events, and sets aside several weeks to obtain a separate Department registration for each vaccinator before opening.
steps: Check the Commissioner's side first. 105 CMR 700.003(F) reaches a vaccine designated by the Commissioner for the prevention of a pandemic, novel, or other vaccine-preventable disease, provided the Commissioner determines that there are or will be insufficient health care professionals available for timely vaccine administration and issues an order authorizing such administration, and 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(a) requires authorization by order of the Commissioner. None of that has happened.

Give the practitioner's instrument its proper weight. Under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(b) administration must be in accordance with the Commissioner's order and the order or prescription of a duly registered practitioner authorized to issue an order or prescription for a vaccine. The medical director's standing prescription is one half of that requirement and does not open the pathway on its own.

Apply the student condition. The paragraph reaches a student duly enrolled in an approved or accredited program for licensure as a health care professional who is acting in accordance with the policies of that program, and 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(c) requires that a student administering vaccine be authorized and supervised by a licensed and qualified health care professional. Unsupervised shifts fail that condition.

Apply the training and supervision duty to everyone who administers. Under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(a) a person administering vaccine shall, in accordance with the Commissioner's order, receive proper training and supervision in the administration of the vaccine. The duty is not confined to students, so licensure does not excuse the pharmacists from it.

Complete the protocols. 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) requires compliance with written protocols to ensure proper storage, handling and return of vaccine, recordkeeping regarding administration, response to adverse events, and safe and appropriate administration of vaccine. A plan limited to storage and adverse events leaves out handling, return, recordkeeping and safe and appropriate administration.

Take registration off the plan's timeline. Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7) a health care professional duly licensed or certified by the Department, or a student duly enrolled in an approved or accredited program for such licensure or certification, who is authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(F) to possess and administer vaccine is exempt from registration for purposes of administering vaccine pursuant to 105 CMR 700.003(F).
worked_examples.resolution: Nothing may be administered under 105 CMR 700.003(F) until the Commissioner has designated the vaccine, made the insufficiency determination and issued the order; after that, administration must follow both the Commissioner's order and a practitioner's order or prescription, students must be authorized and supervised, each person administering must receive proper training and supervision, the protocols must reach every subject the paragraph names, and an authorized vaccinator needs no separate registration for that administration. The error the scenario invites is treating either instrument as a single switch that opens the pathway, and treating licensure as a substitute for the training and supervision the paragraph requires of a person administering.

worked_examples.scenario: A volunteer who coaches a youth sports league wants to buy an over-the-counter naloxone package, keep it in her car, and use it if she ever comes across someone who appears to be overdosing. At the pharmacy counter she asks whether she first needs a Massachusetts registration, or a prescription, to buy, keep and use it.
steps: Identify the product by its package. The Drug Control Program's advisory describes over-the-counter naloxone as sold in FDA-approved packaging for over-the-counter medications and as a separate and distinct product from prescription naloxone, and it states that a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration is not required for activities regarding over-the-counter naloxone.

Answer the registration question from the regulation as well. Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(11) no person shall be required to register with the Department for the purposes of purchasing, storing, possessing, or administering naloxone, or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department.

Answer the prescription question. The advisory describes naloxone as currently available as an over-the-counter medication as well as by prescription, and the over-the-counter package is the product sold without one.

Address use at the scene. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19B(g) a person acting in good faith may possess an opioid antagonist and administer it to an individual appearing to experience an opioid-related overdose, and a person who in good faith administers it is not, as a result of the person's acts or omissions, subject to any criminal or civil liability or any professional disciplinary action; the immunity in s. 34A also applies.
worked_examples.resolution: She needs neither a registration nor a prescription to buy, keep and use the over-the-counter package, and s. 19B(g) protects her good-faith administration. The error the scenario invites is assuming that because naloxone is a medication the Drug Control Program regulates in its prescription form, a member of the public needs a registration or a prescription to carry or use the over-the-counter product.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19(d), to whom may naloxone or other opioid antagonist lawfully be prescribed and dispensed?
retrieval_prompts.answer: To a person at risk of experiencing an opiate-related overdose, or to a family member, friend or other person in a position to assist a person at risk of experiencing an opiate-related overdose.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How is a prescription for an opioid antagonist issued under s. 19(d) regarded for purposes of chapters 94C and 112?
retrieval_prompts.answer: As being issued for a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of professional practice.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Who may issue the statewide opioid antagonist standing order under s. 19B(b), and what must the order include?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Commissioner, or a physician designated by the Commissioner and registered under s. 7 to distribute or dispense a controlled substance in the course of professional practice. The order shall include, but not be limited to, written, standardized procedures or protocols for the dispensing of an opioid antagonist by a licensed pharmacist.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How does the Drug Control Program's advisory tell over-the-counter naloxone from prescription naloxone?
retrieval_prompts.answer: By packaging. Over-the-counter naloxone is sold in FDA-approved packaging for over-the-counter medications; prescription naloxone is sold in FDA-approved packaging which states that federal law prohibits dispensing without a prescription. The advisory treats them as separate and distinct products to which different laws and regulations apply.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: the Drug Control Program's regulations apply to activities regarding over-the-counter naloxone, and a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration is required for those activities.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The advisory states that the Program's regulations do not apply to activities regarding over-the-counter naloxone and do apply to prescription naloxone, and that a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration is not required for activities regarding over-the-counter naloxone.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Is a Department registration required to purchase, store, possess or administer naloxone?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(11) no person shall be required to register with the Department for the purposes of purchasing, storing, possessing, or administering naloxone, or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A grandmother buys naloxone dispensed under the statewide standing order for her grandson and does not ask to pay out-of-pocket. Whose coverage does the pharmacist or designee pursue, and when is the claim submitted?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The grandmother's. Section 19B(e) treats the transaction for health insurance billing and cost-sharing as the dispensing of a prescription to the purchaser regardless of the ultimate user, and requires a reasonable effort to identify her coverage and to submit the claim to the carrier prior to dispensing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What takes away the s. 19B(e) duty to make a reasonable effort to identify coverage and submit a claim?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A request by the person purchasing the opioid antagonist to pay for the prescription out-of-pocket.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What must a pharmacy provide when it dispenses a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist, and when?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet, at the time of dispensing, under 247 CMR 9.06(3). The pamphlet is a Board-approved pamphlet that provides information about an opioid antagonist and responding to an overdose.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does an ordinary over-the-counter naloxone sale engage the counseling and pamphlet duty in 247 CMR 9.06(3)?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. The duty falls on a pharmacy that dispenses, and 247 CMR 2.00 defines dispensing as delivering a drug to an ultimate user pursuant to the lawful order of a practitioner; an over-the-counter sale is made without one. The Department of Public Health's memorandum to retailers says retailers should enable anonymous access to over-the-counter naloxone directly on a shelf. Counseling and the pamphlet come with dispensing on a prescription or under the statewide standing order.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacy has no naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available for dispensing when a requestor asks. What does 247 CMR 9.06(4) require?
retrieval_prompts.answer: It shall refer the requestor to the nearest location that has a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What is a high overdose area, and what does 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) require of a pharmacy located in one?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A geographical area that appears on a list published by the Board, in consultation with the Department of Public Health, of areas with high incidence of opiate overdose. A pharmacy located in one shall maintain a continuous supply of naloxone rescue kits or other approved opioid antagonists readily available for dispensing. The Board's Policy 2024-01 states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths and that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone and maintain a continuous, sufficient supply.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What two provisos does M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C attach to the continuous supply of opioid antagonists?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The continuous supply shall include opioid antagonists approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration to be sold over the counter without a prescription, and such pharmacies shall notify the department if the supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses is insufficient to enable compliance with maintaining a continuous supply.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which pharmacies does s. 19C reach, and who determines the areas concerned?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Pharmacies located in areas with high incidence of opiate overdose, as determined by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy in consultation with the department. The Board's Policy 2024-01 states that since all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone in accordance with s. 19C.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy in a town with few overdoses asks whether it must keep naloxone in stock. What is the answer, and what does it rest on?
retrieval_prompts.answer: It should keep a continuous supply. 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) states the continuous-supply duty for a pharmacy located in a high overdose area, and the Board's Policy 2024-01 states that since all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone in accordance with s. 19C and must maintain a continuous, sufficient supply to meet the needs of the community. The Board's retail compliance inspection report checks that statement.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What label does 247 CMR 9.06(5) require on an opioid antagonist rescue kit that a pharmacy assembles?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A label on the outer package noting "Opioid Antagonist Rescue Kit" or the name of the opioid antagonist followed by "Rescue Kit", and the expiration date, which shall be based on the expiration date of the included unit.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does emergency contraception under s. 19A(a) cover over-the-counter products?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Yes. It means any drug approved by the federal Food and Drug Administration as a contraceptive method for use after sexual intercourse, whether provided over-the-counter or by prescription.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under s. 19A(b), who shall issue the statewide emergency contraception standing order, and how does s. 19B(b) word the corresponding power for opioid antagonists?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Commissioner, or a physician designated by the Commissioner who is registered under s. 7 to distribute or dispense a controlled substance in the course of professional practice, shall issue it. Section 19B(b) says that the Commissioner or such a designated physician may issue the opioid antagonist order; in both sections the department shall ensure that a statewide standing order is issued.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does a COVID-19 control measure mean under s. 19E(a)?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A COVID-19 drug, COVID-19 test or other COVID-19 diagnostic device approved or otherwise authorized by the federal Food and Drug Administration.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Who may issue a standing order under s. 19E(b), and what must its procedures and protocols be consistent with?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Commissioner, or an actively practicing physician who currently prescribes a COVID-19 drug, is designated by the Commissioner and is registered under s. 7 to prescribe or dispense a controlled substance in the course of professional practice. The procedures and protocols shall be consistent with the Food and Drug Administration's revised Emergency Use Authorization for Paxlovid issued July 6, 2022 and declarations issued by the United States Department of Health and Human Services under the federal Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a pharmacist shall complete a Commissioner-approved training program before dispensing emergency contraception under s. 19A.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under s. 19A(d) the pharmacist may complete such a program. The training shall include, but not be limited to, proper documentation, quality assurance and referral to additional services, including appropriate recommendation that the patient follow up with a medical practitioner.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under s. 19E(c), training is mandatory before a pharmacist dispenses which COVID-19 control measure, and what must the program include?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A COVID-19 drug. The program shall include, but not be limited to, evaluation of the patient's medical history and relevant records including recent reports of laboratory blood work to review for kidney or liver problems, clinical considerations relative to contraindications with commonly prescribed medications, recommendations for clinical monitoring for side effects, and appropriate recommendation that the patient follow up with a medical practitioner.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which of the three standing-order regimes states no training requirement for the pharmacist?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The opioid antagonist regime: neither s. 19B nor 247 CMR 9.06 contains one. Section 19B(b) instead requires the statewide standing order to include written, standardized procedures or protocols for dispensing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which standing-order regime reports upon request rather than annually, and on what?
retrieval_prompts.answer: COVID-19 control measures: under s. 19E(d) the pharmacist reports, upon request, on the doses, tests or devices dispensed. Emergency contraception under s. 19A(e) and opioid antagonists under s. 19B(d) are reported annually.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an opioid antagonist report filed under s. 19B(d) becomes a public record once the department receives it.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The report shall not identify an individual patient, shall be confidential and shall not constitute a public record as defined in clause Twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4. The department separately publishes an annual report of aggregate information.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under the Board's Policy 2024-01, how does a pharmacy report the naloxone doses it dispenses?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Preferably with its daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, which are for data collection only and do not appear on a patient's profile in the program. A pharmacy that chooses not to report that way must email an annual report by January 15 giving, for the previous calendar year, its name and zip code, the total number of naloxone doses dispensed (not prescriptions or manufacturer-supplied units) and the number of those doses paid for with insurance.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which of the three reporting provisions does not contain the sentence that reports shall not identify an individual patient?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Section 19E(d), for COVID-19 control measures. Its reports are still confidential and are not a public record under clause Twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4. The sentence appears in s. 19A(e) and s. 19B(d).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under 105 CMR 700.003(F), what must the Commissioner have done before a health care professional or student may possess and administer vaccine under that paragraph?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Designated the vaccine for the prevention of a pandemic, novel, or other vaccine-preventable disease, determined that there are or will be insufficient health care professionals available for timely vaccine administration, and issued an order authorizing such administration.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: once the Commissioner's order is issued under 105 CMR 700.003(F), a practitioner's order or prescription is no longer needed.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(b) administration must be in accordance with the Commissioner's order and the order or prescription of a duly registered practitioner authorized to issue an order or prescription for a vaccine.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What conditions attach to a student who administers vaccine under 105 CMR 700.003(F)?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The student must be duly enrolled in an approved or accredited program for licensure as a health care professional and acting in accordance with the policies of that program, and under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(c) must be authorized and supervised by a licensed and qualified health care professional.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the subjects the written protocols under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) must ensure.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Proper storage, handling and return of vaccine; recordkeeping regarding administration; response to adverse events; and safe and appropriate administration of vaccine.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does the training-and-supervision duty in 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(a) apply only to students?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. It applies to a person administering vaccine, in accordance with the Commissioner's order. The separate student condition, authorization and supervision by a licensed and qualified health care professional, sits in 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(c).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does a person authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(F) to possess and administer vaccine need a Department registration to administer vaccine under that paragraph?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7) exempts a health care professional duly licensed or certified by the Department, or a student duly enrolled in an approved or accredited program for such licensure or certification, who is so authorized, from registration for purposes of administering vaccine pursuant to 105 CMR 700.003(F).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What protection does s. 19B(c) give a pharmacist who dispenses an opioid antagonist, and what does it not cover?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A pharmacist who, acting in good faith, dispenses an opioid antagonist is not subject to any criminal or civil liability or any professional disciplinary action by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy related to the use or administration of an opioid antagonist. The protection does not cover an act of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What may a person acting in good faith do with an opioid antagonist under s. 19B(g)?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Receive a prescription for an opioid antagonist, possess an opioid antagonist, and administer it to an individual appearing to experience an opioid-related overdose.

quick_review.text: Under s. 19(d) naloxone or other opioid antagonist may lawfully be prescribed and dispensed to a person at risk of experiencing an opiate-related overdose or to a family member, friend or other person in a position to assist, and such a prescription is regarded as issued for a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of professional practice.

The department shall ensure that a statewide standing order authorizes any licensed pharmacist to dispense an opioid antagonist; the Commissioner or a designated physician registered under s. 7 may issue it, and it includes written, standardized procedures or protocols for dispensing.

Over-the-counter and prescription naloxone are separate and distinct products identified by their FDA-approved packaging; the Drug Control Program's regulations apply to activities regarding the prescription product and not to those regarding the over-the-counter one.
Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(11) no person shall be required to register with the Department to purchase, store, possess or administer naloxone or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department.

Under s. 19B(e) an opioid antagonist dispensed under s. 19B is treated for billing and cost-sharing as a prescription dispensed to the purchaser regardless of the ultimate user, with a reasonable effort to submit the purchaser's claim prior to dispensing unless the purchaser asks to pay out-of-pocket.
A pharmacy that dispenses a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist provides counseling and the Board-approved opioid antagonist information pamphlet at the time of dispensing.

Counseling and the pamphlet under 247 CMR 9.06(3) attach to dispensing, which 247 CMR 2.00 ties to delivery pursuant to the lawful order of a practitioner; Department guidance asks retailers to enable anonymous open-shelf access to over-the-counter naloxone.
A pharmacy without a kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available for dispensing at the time requested refers the requestor to the nearest location that has one readily available.

A pharmacy located in a high overdose area maintains a continuous supply of naloxone rescue kits or other approved opioid antagonists readily available for dispensing, and the Board's Policy 2024-01 states that since all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone and maintain a continuous, sufficient supply; a pharmacy that assembles rescue kits labels the outer package with the kit name and an expiration date based on the included unit.

Under s. 19C the continuous supply of opioid antagonists in areas with high incidence of opiate overdose shall include opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription, and such pharmacies shall notify the department if the supply or stock of doses is insufficient to maintain it. The Board's Policy 2024-01 states that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone in accordance with s. 19C.

Section 19B protects a good-faith dispensing pharmacist, the issuer of the standing order and a good-faith prescribing or dispensing practitioner except for gross negligence or willful misconduct, and protects a person who in good faith administers an opioid antagonist to an individual appearing to experience an opioid-related overdose.

Emergency contraception under s. 19A(a) includes drugs provided over-the-counter or by prescription, and the Commissioner or a designated physician registered under s. 7 shall issue the statewide standing order that the department shall ensure is issued.

A COVID-19 control measure under s. 19E(a) is a COVID-19 drug, test or other diagnostic device approved or otherwise authorized by the FDA, and the Commissioner, or an actively practicing physician who currently prescribes a COVID-19 drug, is designated by the Commissioner and is registered under s. 7, may issue the s. 19E(b) standing order.
Emergency contraception training under s. 19A(d) is permissive; COVID-19 drug training under s. 19E(c) is mandatory before dispensing a COVID-19 drug.
Neither s. 19B nor 247 CMR 9.06 states a training requirement for dispensing an opioid antagonist.
Emergency contraception and opioid antagonist dispensing are reported annually; COVID-19 control measures are reported upon request, on the doses, tests or devices dispensed.

Under the Board's Policy 2024-01 each Massachusetts pharmacy reports naloxone doses dispensed, preferably with its daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, or otherwise by an emailed annual report due by January 15 for the previous calendar year.

All three reporting provisions make the reports confidential and keep them outside the public-records definition; s. 19A(e) and s. 19B(d) add that reports shall not identify an individual patient, and s. 19E(d) does not.

Under 105 CMR 700.003(F) administration of a Commissioner-designated vaccine depends on the Commissioner's insufficiency determination and authorizing order, and must accord with both that order and a duly registered practitioner's order or prescription.
A student may administer under 105 CMR 700.003(F) while acting in accordance with the program's policies and when authorized and supervised by a licensed and qualified health care professional.

A person administering vaccine under the Commissioner's order receives proper training and supervision and complies with written protocols on storage, handling and return of vaccine, recordkeeping regarding administration, response to adverse events, and safe and appropriate administration.

A health care professional or student authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(F) to possess and administer vaccine is exempt under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7) from registration for purposes of administering vaccine under that paragraph.

decision_logic.condition: Someone asks for an opioid antagonist for another person who is not present.
decision_logic.action: Treat the request as within the law: s. 19(d) allows prescribing and dispensing to a family member, friend or other person in a position to assist a person at risk of experiencing an opiate-related overdose, and under s. 19B(c) a licensed pharmacist may dispense in accordance with the statewide standing order.

decision_logic.condition: The legal category of a naloxone package is in doubt.
decision_logic.action: Read the FDA-approved packaging. Packaging for over-the-counter medications marks over-the-counter naloxone, to which the Drug Control Program's regulations do not apply; packaging stating that federal law prohibits dispensing without a prescription marks prescription naloxone, which the advisory describes as a medication that cannot be dispensed without a prescription or standing order.

decision_logic.condition: A member of the public asks whether a registration is needed to buy, keep or use naloxone.
decision_logic.action: Answer from 105 CMR 700.004(B)(11): no person shall be required to register with the Department for the purposes of purchasing, storing, possessing, or administering naloxone, or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department.

decision_logic.condition: An opioid antagonist is to be dispensed under s. 19B and the purchaser has not asked to pay out-of-pocket.
decision_logic.action: Treat the transaction as a prescription dispensed to the purchaser, look to the purchaser's coverage rather than the ultimate user's, and make a reasonable effort to submit the claim to that carrier prior to dispensing.

decision_logic.condition: The purchaser asks to pay out-of-pocket.
decision_logic.action: The reasonable-effort duty to identify coverage and submit a claim does not arise, because s. 19B(e) states it as applying unless the purchaser makes that request.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy dispenses a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist.
decision_logic.action: Provide counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet at the time of dispensing; the regulation requires both, so one does not substitute for the other.

decision_logic.condition: A customer buys an over-the-counter naloxone package without a prescription or the standing order.
decision_logic.action: Treat it as a sale, not dispensing: 247 CMR 2.00 defines dispensing by delivery pursuant to the lawful order of a practitioner, so the counseling and pamphlet duty in 247 CMR 9.06(3) is not engaged, and the Department's memorandum asks retailers to enable anonymous access to over-the-counter naloxone directly on a shelf. When naloxone is dispensed on a prescription or under the statewide standing order, provide counseling and the pamphlet.

decision_logic.condition: No kit or other approved opioid antagonist is readily available for dispensing when one is requested.
decision_logic.action: Refer the requestor to the nearest location that has one readily available. Recognize separately that 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) requires a pharmacy located in a high overdose area to maintain a continuous supply readily available for dispensing and that the Board's Policy 2024-01 states that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone and maintain a continuous, sufficient supply, and notify the department under s. 19C if the supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses is insufficient to enable compliance with maintaining a continuous supply.

decision_logic.condition: A Massachusetts pharmacy is setting up its naloxone stock.
decision_logic.action: Keep a continuous, sufficient supply of naloxone rescue kits or other approved opioid antagonists readily available for dispensing, as 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) and the Board's Policy 2024-01 provide, and include in it opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription, as s. 19C provides. Do not treat the pharmacy's location as excusing it: the Board's policy states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy assembles its own opioid antagonist rescue kits.
decision_logic.action: Label the outer package "Opioid Antagonist Rescue Kit" or with the name of the opioid antagonist followed by "Rescue Kit", with an expiration date based on the expiration date of the included unit.

decision_logic.condition: It is unclear which standing order, and which issuer, stands behind a pharmacist's dispensing.
decision_logic.action: Identify the regime. Emergency contraception: the statewide standing order that the Commissioner or a designated physician registered under s. 7 shall issue under s. 19A(b). Opioid antagonist: the statewide standing order that the Commissioner or such a physician may issue under s. 19B(b). COVID-19 control measure: a standing order under s. 19E(b) issued by the Commissioner or by an actively practicing physician who currently prescribes a COVID-19 drug, is designated by the Commissioner and is registered under s. 7.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist who has completed no training program wants to dispense under a standing order.
decision_logic.action: Identify the regime. For emergency contraception under s. 19A the training is permissive. For a COVID-19 drug under s. 19E the Commissioner-approved program on COVID-19 drugs comes first. For an opioid antagonist under s. 19B neither the statute nor 247 CMR 9.06 states a training requirement.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist is working out when standing-order reports fall due.
decision_logic.action: Report emergency contraception and opioid antagonist dispensing annually, and report on COVID-19 doses, tests or devices dispensed upon the department's request.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy is setting up its naloxone dose reporting.
decision_logic.action: Report through the pharmacy's daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, the method the Board's Policy 2024-01 prefers, or, if the pharmacy chooses not to, email the annual report by January 15 with the pharmacy's name and zip code, the total naloxone doses dispensed in the previous calendar year and the number of those doses paid for with insurance, without identifying an individual patient, as s. 19B(d) requires of the reports.

decision_logic.condition: A standing-order report is being prepared or requested.
decision_logic.action: Keep emergency contraception and opioid antagonist reports free of individual patient identification, and treat the reports in all three regimes as confidential and outside the public-records definition.

decision_logic.condition: A clinic proposes to administer vaccine under 105 CMR 700.003(F).
decision_logic.action: Check the Commissioner's side first: a designated vaccine, a determination that there are or will be insufficient health care professionals available for timely vaccine administration, and an order authorizing administration. Then check the practitioner's side: administration in accordance with the order or prescription of a duly registered practitioner authorized to issue one for a vaccine, as well as with the Commissioner's order.

decision_logic.condition: A student is to administer vaccine under the Commissioner's order.
decision_logic.action: Confirm enrollment in an approved or accredited program for licensure as a health care professional, action in accordance with that program's policies, and authorization and supervision by a licensed and qualified health care professional.

decision_logic.condition: Staff administer vaccine under the Commissioner's order.
decision_logic.action: Each person administering shall receive proper training and supervision in the administration of the vaccine and shall comply with written protocols to ensure proper storage, handling and return of vaccine, recordkeeping regarding administration, response to adverse events, and safe and appropriate administration.

decision_logic.condition: Vaccinators authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(F) ask whether they must first register with the Department.
decision_logic.action: No registration is needed for administering vaccine pursuant to 105 CMR 700.003(F): 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7) exempts a health care professional duly licensed or certified by the Department, or a student duly enrolled in an approved or accredited program for such licensure or certification, who is authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(F) to possess and administer vaccine.

ma_vs_federal.text: Federal approval sets the product line the Massachusetts advisory follows: the FDA has approved naloxone to be sold over the counter while naloxone continues to be available by prescription, and the Drug Control Program uses the FDA-approved packaging to separate over-the-counter naloxone, outside the Program's regulations, from prescription naloxone, which remains within them.

The Massachusetts definition of an opioid antagonist in s. 19B(a) and 247 CMR 9.06(1)(c) is tied to federal approval: naloxone or any other drug approved by the federal Food and Drug Administration as a competitive narcotic antagonist used in the reversal of overdoses caused by opioids.

The over-the-counter part of the continuous supply in s. 19C is defined by federal approval: opioid antagonists approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration to be sold over the counter without a prescription.

Emergency contraception under s. 19A(a) is defined by federal approval: any drug approved by the federal Food and Drug Administration as a contraceptive method for use after sexual intercourse, whether provided over-the-counter or by prescription.

Section 19E ties its standing order to federal instruments: a COVID-19 control measure is a drug, test or diagnostic device approved or otherwise authorized by the FDA, and the order's procedures and protocols shall be consistent with the FDA's revised Emergency Use Authorization for Paxlovid issued July 6, 2022 and with declarations issued by the United States Department of Health and Human Services under the federal Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act.

exceptions.text: The s. 19B(e) duty to make a reasonable effort to identify the purchaser's coverage and submit a claim prior to dispensing does not arise when the purchaser requests to pay for the prescription out-of-pocket.

The protections in s. 19B(c) for a dispensing pharmacist and in s. 19B(f) for the issuer of the standing order and for prescribing or dispensing practitioners do not cover an act of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

The continuous-supply duty in 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) is stated for a pharmacy located in a high overdose area, and 247 CMR 9.06(2)(b) provides that a pharmacy not located in one may dispense under the statewide standing order or a prescription if it complies with all other provisions of 247 CMR 9.06. The Board's Policy 2024-01 states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths and that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone and maintain a continuous, sufficient supply, so no Massachusetts pharmacy should rely on that wording to go without stock.

An ordinary over-the-counter naloxone sale, made without a practitioner's order, is not dispensing as 247 CMR 2.00 defines it, so the counseling and pamphlet duty that 247 CMR 9.06(3) places on a pharmacy that dispenses does not attach to it.

Among the exemptions from the requirement to register in 105 CMR 700.004(B), paragraph (B)(11) provides that no person shall be required to register with the Department for the purposes of purchasing, storing, possessing, or administering naloxone, or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department.
Emergency contraception training under s. 19A(d) is permissive, so s. 19A does not make completion of the training a condition of dispensing; the content the training shall include is still stated.
The mandatory training in s. 19E(c) is stated as a condition of dispensing a COVID-19 drug; the proviso does not name COVID-19 tests or devices.
105 CMR 700.003(F) applies notwithstanding any other Department regulation.

The student route under 105 CMR 700.003(F) carries a condition the licensed professional's route does not: authorization and supervision by a licensed and qualified health care professional under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(c).

A health care professional or student authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(F) to possess and administer vaccine is exempt under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7) from registration for purposes of administering vaccine pursuant to that paragraph.

timing_deadlines.event: Insurance claim for an opioid antagonist dispensed under s. 19B
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Prior to dispensing, unless the purchaser requests to pay out-of-pocket
timing_deadlines.consequence: The pharmacist or designee makes a reasonable effort to identify the purchaser's coverage and submit the claim before the opioid antagonist is handed over.

timing_deadlines.event: Counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet
timing_deadlines.consequence: The pharmacy that dispenses the kit or other approved opioid antagonist provides both at that point.

timing_deadlines.event: Request for a kit when none is readily available for dispensing
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Availability is judged at the time requested
timing_deadlines.consequence: The pharmacy refers the requestor to the nearest location that has one readily available.

timing_deadlines.event: Naloxone stock in a Massachusetts pharmacy
timing_deadlines.consequence: 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) requires a pharmacy located in a high overdose area to maintain naloxone rescue kits or other approved opioid antagonists readily available for dispensing; the Board's Policy 2024-01 states that Massachusetts pharmacies must maintain a continuous, sufficient supply because all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths; and under s. 19C the continuous supply includes opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription.

timing_deadlines.event: Supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses insufficient to maintain a continuous supply
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No period is stated; the duty arises if the supply or stock is insufficient
timing_deadlines.consequence: A pharmacy located in an area with high incidence of opiate overdose notifies the department under s. 19C; the Board's Policy 2024-01 states that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone in accordance with s. 19C, so every Massachusetts pharmacy should give the notice.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Before dispensing, where the pharmacist chooses to complete it
timing_deadlines.consequence: The training is permissive under s. 19A(d), and it shall include documentation, quality assurance and referral to additional services.
The pharmacist shall complete the Commissioner-approved training program on COVID-19 drugs under s. 19E(c).
The dispensing pharmacist provides the department with the number of times emergency contraception is dispensed.

The dispensing pharmacist reports to the department the number of opioid antagonist doses dispensed under s. 19B(d); the Board's Policy 2024-01 has the pharmacy make the naloxone report through its daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions or by an emailed annual report.

timing_deadlines.event: Emailed annual naloxone report under the Board's Policy 2024-01
timing_deadlines.timeframe: By January 15, covering the previous calendar year
timing_deadlines.consequence: Required of a pharmacy that chooses not to report naloxone dispensing through its daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions; it gives the pharmacy's name and zip code, the total naloxone doses dispensed and the number of those doses paid for with insurance.
The dispensing pharmacist reports on the doses, tests or devices dispensed; s. 19E(d) sets no annual cycle for the pharmacist's report.
The department publishes aggregate information about opioid antagonist dispensing under s. 19B(d) and about COVID-19 control measures under s. 19E(d); s. 19A has no counterpart.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Once the Commissioner has designated the vaccine, made the insufficiency determination and issued the authorizing order
timing_deadlines.consequence: Before then, a practitioner's order or prescription does not by itself authorize administration under the paragraph.

forms_records.text: The statewide opioid antagonist standing order shall include, but not be limited to, written, standardized procedures or protocols for the dispensing of an opioid antagonist by a licensed pharmacist.

The statewide emergency contraception standing order shall include, but not be limited to, written, standardized procedures or protocols for the dispensing of emergency contraception by a licensed pharmacist.

A COVID-19 standing order shall include written standardized procedures or protocols developed by the Commissioner in collaboration with an actively practicing physician who currently prescribes a COVID-19 drug, consistent with the revised Emergency Use Authorization for Paxlovid issued July 6, 2022 and federal Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act declarations.

The opioid antagonist information pamphlet is a Board-approved pamphlet that provides information about an opioid antagonist and responding to an overdose, and the dispensing pharmacy provides it with counseling at the time of dispensing.

247 CMR 9.06(1)(a) ties a high overdose area to a list published by the Board in consultation with the Department of Public Health, but the Board's Policy 2024-01 states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths and that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone, and the Board's retail compliance inspection report checks that statement, citing 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) and (b) and the policy; a Massachusetts pharmacy should not wait to find its town on a list before keeping naloxone in stock.
Section 19C calls for a notice to the department when the supply or stock of opioid antagonist doses is insufficient to enable compliance with maintaining a continuous supply.

An opioid antagonist rescue kit assembled by a pharmacy carries an outer-package label noting "Opioid Antagonist Rescue Kit" or the name of the opioid antagonist followed by "Rescue Kit", and an expiration date based on the expiration date of the included unit.

The FDA-approved packaging identifies which naloxone product is in hand: packaging for over-the-counter medications for the over-the-counter product, and packaging stating that federal law prohibits dispensing without a prescription for the prescription product.

For an opioid antagonist dispensed under s. 19B, the claim goes to the purchaser's insurance carrier as for a prescription dispensed to the purchaser, prior to dispensing, unless the purchaser requests to pay out-of-pocket.

The opioid antagonist report states the number of doses dispensed, the emergency contraception report the number of times emergency contraception is dispensed, and the COVID-19 report, when requested, the doses, tests or devices dispensed.

Under the Board's Policy 2024-01 the naloxone dose report goes preferably with the pharmacy's daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, for data collection only and not shown on a patient's profile in the program; otherwise the pharmacy emails an annual report by January 15 with its name and zip code, the total naloxone doses dispensed in the previous calendar year (not prescriptions or manufacturer-supplied units) and the number of those doses paid for with insurance, and details of each dispensing event (doses, date, the recipient's zip code of residence and insurance payment) are encouraged but not required.

Standing-order reports are confidential and are not public records; those under s. 19A(e) and s. 19B(d) shall not identify an individual patient, and the department's published annual reports under s. 19B(d) and s. 19E(d) contain aggregate information.
The training programs in s. 19A(d) and s. 19E(c) are programs approved by the Commissioner, on emergency contraception and on COVID-19 drugs respectively.

Two instruments govern emergency administration under 105 CMR 700.003(F): the Commissioner's order authorizing administration, and the order or prescription of a duly registered practitioner authorized to issue an order or prescription for a vaccine.

Written protocols under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) ensure proper storage, handling and return of vaccine, recordkeeping regarding administration, response to adverse events, and safe and appropriate administration of vaccine.

role_duties.role: Department of Public Health
role_duties.duty: Ensure that a statewide standing order is issued to authorize the dispensing of an opioid antagonist in the Commonwealth by any licensed pharmacist, and likewise a statewide standing order to authorize the dispensing of emergency contraception by a licensed pharmacist.

role_duties.role: Commissioner, or a physician designated by the Commissioner and registered under s. 7, for opioid antagonists
role_duties.duty: May issue the statewide opioid antagonist standing order, which shall include written, standardized procedures or protocols for dispensing by a licensed pharmacist.

role_duties.role: Commissioner, or a physician designated by the Commissioner and registered under s. 7, for emergency contraception
role_duties.duty: Shall issue the statewide emergency contraception standing order, which shall include written, standardized procedures or protocols for dispensing by a licensed pharmacist.

role_duties.role: Commissioner, or an actively practicing physician who currently prescribes a COVID-19 drug, is designated by the Commissioner and is registered under s. 7
role_duties.duty: May issue a standing order for a licensed pharmacist to dispense COVID-19 control measures; its procedures and protocols are developed by the Commissioner in collaboration with an actively practicing physician who currently prescribes a COVID-19 drug and shall be consistent with the revised Emergency Use Authorization for Paxlovid issued July 6, 2022 and federal Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act declarations.

role_duties.role: Licensed pharmacist dispensing an opioid antagonist
role_duties.duty: May dispense in accordance with the statewide standing order, and shall annually report to the department the number of opioid antagonist doses dispensed, in reports that shall not identify an individual patient.

role_duties.role: Massachusetts pharmacy dispensing naloxone, under the Board's Policy 2024-01
role_duties.duty: Report the number of naloxone doses dispensed, preferably with daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, or, if the pharmacy chooses not to report that way, by an emailed annual report due by January 15 for the previous calendar year.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist or designee
role_duties.duty: For an opioid antagonist dispensed under s. 19B, treat the transaction as a prescription dispensed to the purchaser and, unless the purchaser requests to pay out-of-pocket, make a reasonable effort to identify the purchaser's coverage and submit a claim prior to dispensing.

role_duties.role: Pharmacy dispensing a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist
role_duties.duty: Provide counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet at the time of dispensing.

role_duties.role: Pharmacy without a kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available at the time requested
role_duties.duty: Refer the requestor to the nearest location that has a naloxone rescue kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available.

role_duties.role: Massachusetts pharmacy keeping naloxone stock
role_duties.duty: Maintain a continuous, sufficient supply of naloxone rescue kits or other approved opioid antagonists readily available for dispensing, as 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) requires of a pharmacy in a high overdose area and as the Board's Policy 2024-01 states is required of Massachusetts pharmacies because all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths; include opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription in that supply as s. 19C provides; and notify the department if the supply or stock of doses is insufficient to maintain it.

role_duties.role: Pharmacy that assembles opioid antagonist rescue kits
role_duties.duty: Affix the required label to the outer package, with an expiration date based on the expiration date of the included unit.

role_duties.role: Board of Registration in Pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Approve the opioid antagonist information pamphlet, and publish, in consultation with the Department of Public Health, the list of high overdose areas; in its Policy 2024-01 the Board states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths.

role_duties.role: Board of Registration in Pharmacy, under s. 19C
role_duties.duty: Promulgate regulations requiring pharmacies located in areas with high incidence of opiate overdose, as determined by the Board in consultation with the department, to maintain a continuous supply of opioid antagonists.

role_duties.role: Person acting in good faith at an overdose
role_duties.duty: May receive a prescription for, possess and administer an opioid antagonist to an individual appearing to experience an opioid-related overdose, and is not subject to criminal or civil liability or professional disciplinary action as a result of the person's acts or omissions in administering it.

role_duties.role: Any person purchasing, storing, possessing or administering naloxone
role_duties.duty: Is not required to register with the Department for those purposes, under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(11), where the product is naloxone or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department.

role_duties.role: Retailer selling over-the-counter naloxone
role_duties.duty: Enable anonymous access to naloxone directly on a shelf, without locking it behind a cabinet or in a container that requires contacting an employee, as the Department's memorandum to retailers says retailers should.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist dispensing emergency contraception under s. 19A
role_duties.duty: May dispense in accordance with the statewide standing order, may complete a Commissioner-approved training program before dispensing, and shall annually provide the department with the number of times emergency contraception is dispensed.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist dispensing a COVID-19 control measure under a standing order
role_duties.duty: Complete the Commissioner-approved training program on COVID-19 drugs before dispensing a COVID-19 drug, and report to the department upon request on the doses, tests or devices dispensed.

role_duties.role: Department of Public Health, as recipient of standing-order reports
role_duties.duty: Publish annual reports with aggregate information about opioid antagonist dispensing and about the dispensing of COVID-19 control measures; the reports it receives under s. 19A(e), s. 19B(d) and s. 19E(d) are confidential and are not public records.

role_duties.role: Commissioner of Public Health, for emergency vaccination
role_duties.duty: Designate the vaccine, determine whether there are or will be insufficient health care professionals available for timely vaccine administration, and issue the order authorizing administration under 105 CMR 700.003(F).

role_duties.role: Duly registered practitioner authorized to issue an order or prescription for a vaccine
role_duties.duty: Supply the order or prescription with which administration under 105 CMR 700.003(F) must accord alongside the Commissioner's order.

role_duties.role: Health care professional duly licensed or certified by the Department
role_duties.duty: Administer a designated vaccine in accordance with the Commissioner's order and a practitioner's order or prescription, receive proper training and supervision in administration, and comply with the written protocols; a professional so authorized is exempt from registration for that administration under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7).

role_duties.role: Student duly enrolled in an approved or accredited program for licensure as a health care professional
role_duties.duty: Act in accordance with the program's policies, administer when authorized and supervised by a licensed and qualified health care professional, and meet the training, supervision and protocol duties that apply to a person administering vaccine; a student so authorized is exempt from registration for that administration under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7).

role_duties.role: Licensed and qualified health care professional overseeing a student
role_duties.duty: Authorize and supervise the student who administers vaccine under 105 CMR 700.003(F).

common_traps.text: Refusing an opioid antagonist to a family member, friend or other person in a position to assist because the person at risk is not present. Section 19(d) expressly allows prescribing and dispensing to such a person.

Treating over-the-counter naloxone and prescription naloxone as one product category. The Drug Control Program's advisory treats them as separate and distinct products, identified by their FDA-approved packaging, to which different laws and regulations apply.

Assuming a registration with the Department is needed to purchase, store, possess or administer naloxone. 105 CMR 700.004(B)(11) provides that no person shall be required to register for those purposes.
Billing the ultimate user's plan, or submitting the claim after the opioid antagonist has been handed over. Section 19B(e) looks to the purchaser's coverage and to a claim prior to dispensing.

Telling a purchaser who buys for someone else that the purchase must be paid in cash. Section 19B(e) treats the purchase as a prescription dispensed to the purchaser regardless of the ultimate user, and paying out-of-pocket is the purchaser's election.

Treating a stock-out as the end of the pharmacy's obligations, or inviting the requestor to come back later. 247 CMR 9.06(4) requires a referral to the nearest location that has a kit or other approved opioid antagonist readily available.
Treating spoken counseling as satisfying the pamphlet requirement, or the pamphlet as satisfying counseling. 247 CMR 9.06(3) requires both at the time of dispensing.

Treating counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet as required on an ordinary over-the-counter naloxone sale. 247 CMR 9.06(3) attaches them to dispensing, which 247 CMR 2.00 defines by delivery pursuant to the lawful order of a practitioner, and the Department's memorandum asks retailers to enable anonymous shelf access to over-the-counter naloxone.

Assuming that a Massachusetts pharmacy has done all it must once it refers a requestor elsewhere. The referral in 247 CMR 9.06(4) does not supply the continuous stock that 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) and the Board's Policy 2024-01 call for, and s. 19C provides that such pharmacies shall notify the department when the supply or stock of doses is insufficient.

Treating a pharmacy in a town with comparatively few overdoses as free of the continuous-supply duty because the town is not on a list of high overdose areas. The Board's Policy 2024-01 states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths and that Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone and maintain a continuous, sufficient supply.

Treating over-the-counter opioid antagonists as outside the continuous supply. Section 19C provides that the continuous supply shall include opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription.

Limiting emergency contraception to prescription products. Section 19A(a) defines it as any FDA-approved drug for use as a contraceptive method after sexual intercourse, whether provided over-the-counter or by prescription.

Carrying the word may from s. 19B(b) into s. 19A(b). The Commissioner or designated physician shall issue the statewide emergency contraception standing order, while s. 19B(b) says may for the opioid antagonist order.
Limiting a COVID-19 control measure to drugs. Section 19E(a) also covers COVID-19 tests and other COVID-19 diagnostic devices, and the s. 19E(d) report reaches the doses, tests or devices dispensed.

Assuming one training rule governs every standing order. Emergency contraception training is permissive, COVID-19 drug training is mandatory, and neither s. 19B nor 247 CMR 9.06 states a training requirement for opioid antagonists.
Treating the COVID-19 training as optional, or reading its proviso as reaching tests and devices. Section 19E(c) makes the training mandatory before dispensing a COVID-19 drug.
Putting all three regimes on an annual reporting cycle. The pharmacist's report on COVID-19 control measures under s. 19E(d) is made upon request.

Assuming s. 19E(d) contains the sentence that reports shall not identify an individual patient. That sentence appears in s. 19A(e) and s. 19B(d); s. 19E(d) makes its reports confidential and not a public record without repeating it.
Treating standing-order reports as public records because they are filed with a state agency. Each reporting provision makes them confidential and excludes them from the public-records definition.

Counting prescriptions or manufacturer-supplied units in the naloxone report, or assuming that naloxone reported through the Prescription Monitoring Program appears on a patient's profile. The Board's Policy 2024-01 counts naloxone doses and says the program submission is for data collection only.

Treating a practitioner's standing prescription as enough to administer a designated vaccine without the Commissioner's order, or the Commissioner's order as removing the need for a practitioner's order or prescription.

Treating the training-and-supervision duty in 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(a) as a student-only condition. It applies to a person administering vaccine; the student-specific condition is authorization and supervision under 105 CMR 700.003(F)(1)(c).

Dropping return of vaccine or recordkeeping from the written protocols. 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) names storage, handling and return of vaccine, recordkeeping regarding administration, response to adverse events, and safe and appropriate administration.

Assuming vaccinators authorized under 105 CMR 700.003(F) need their own Department registration. 105 CMR 700.004(B)(7) exempts them from registration for purposes of administering vaccine pursuant to that paragraph.
Reading the pharmacist's protection in s. 19B(c) as reaching gross negligence or willful misconduct. Both are expressly excepted.

drug_examples.teaching_point: Prescription naloxone is sold in FDA-approved packaging which states that federal law prohibits dispensing without a prescription, and the advisory describes it as a medication that cannot be dispensed without a prescription or standing order. When a pharmacy dispenses it, 247 CMR 9.06(3) requires counseling and the opioid antagonist information pamphlet, and when it is dispensed under s. 19B the purchaser-billing rule in s. 19B(e) applies.

Over-the-counter naloxone is sold in FDA-approved packaging for over-the-counter medications and is a separate and distinct product from prescription naloxone; the Drug Control Program's regulations do not apply to activities regarding it, and no Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration is required for those activities. Under s. 19C the continuous supply, which the Board's Policy 2024-01 states is required of Massachusetts pharmacies, shall include opioid antagonists approved to be sold over the counter without a prescription, and the Department's memorandum to retailers says over-the-counter naloxone should be available for anonymous purchase directly on a shelf.
